layers.note: The tree of the south Puget Sound prairies and oak woodlands, and of dry, rocky slopes.

moisture.note: Dry ground: prairie edges, gravelly outwash and rocky slopes.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Holds dry slopes and bluffs as well as flats.

shade_tolerance.note: Shade intolerant: Douglas-fir overtops and kills it where fires no longer burn.

coldest_c.note: Mild winters: coldest-month means from about −2 °C (gone by −6 °C), as in the Puget Trough, the Willamette Valley and the foothills of California.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −22 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −30 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warm, dry summers: warmest-month means from about 15.5 to 27 °C, gone below 13 °C and above 30.5 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long warm season: about 3,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 2,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,600 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,100: it stays in warm lowlands and on the lower slopes.

moisture_index.note: Summer drought borne: a moisture index from about 0.32 (gone by 0.2), dry savanna and prairie climates included.

summer_rain.note: A Mediterranean-type climate: its range lies where at most about 0.2 of the year's precipitation falls in summer, gone by 0.35.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Oregon white oak grows from Vancouver Island to the foothills of central California, the only native oak of Washington, on prairie edges and dry slopes (Silvics of North America, vol. 2). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
